page_title: Pixtamer: free batch image optimiser for Mac

sources.entry: Pixtamer - Batch convert, compress, resize and rename images into web-ready JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF, with responsive widths and presets. Nothing is uploaded. summary.name: Pixtamer
summary.one_liner: Pixtamer is a free, native Mac app that batch converts, compresses, resizes and renames images into web-ready JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF files, all processed locally.
use_cases: Prepare photos for a website in several widths
Convert a folder of iPhone photos to WebP
Generate srcset image files for responsive layouts
Rename exported images for web use
Resize large images without uploading them
summary.what_it_does: Pixtamer applies a saved recipe or preset to every file in a batch, converting format, resizing, compressing and renaming in one run. It can export one file per chosen width, named for use in srcset markup, and does not upscale small images. Originals are left untouched, each export is a new file, and existing files are not overwritten unless chosen. A before/after comparison view lets you check results at fit or 100%. The page says nothing leaves the Mac: there is no account, analytics, upload or network access.
notable: Runs entirely on the Mac with no uploads and no network access, sandboxed by macOS
Responsive export: one file per width, named for srcset use
Open source on GitHub and available on the Mac App Store
Before/after comparison and real measured file sizes
caveats: Mac only; no Windows or Linux version is mentioned
RAW and PSD files are not accepted
AVIF export appears only if the Mac's encoder passes a test at launch
Animated GIFs export only their first frame; 16-bit and HDR images export as 8-bit
